qt: to the Commission Benoit Cassart (Renew) Subject:

In 2025, the EU imported 9.7 million tonnes of waste and residue for biodiesel production – an increase of 350 % in 10 years. The vast majority of these imports came from China, Indonesia and Malaysia. A significant number were falsely declared as falling under Annex IX to the Renewable Energy Directive, thereby allowing importers to take unfair advantage of EU incentives, at the expense of European biofuels, which are vital for the energy and protein sovereignty of our companies. After serious flaws were identified in the ISCC voluntary certification scheme, the Commission had considered suspending its recognition of imports certified under the scheme in China, but to date it has not taken any concrete action. In light of the above: 1.
Can the Commission share its latest quantitative and qualitative assessment of the scale of this fraud and the structural flaws in the ISCC system?
For what legal or political reasons has it not yet suspended recognition of imports certified under the ISCC scheme in China, despite having previously contemplated doing so?
What emergency measures will it take to protect the internal market from these distortions of competition, and safeguard the integrity of the Union database in response to these fraudulent imports?
